# A handler that reads the loop variable of the loop its node is in.
#
# A promoted top-level handler cannot see one -- it is written outside the
# loop -- so the handler is attached as a closure instead, which captures it.
# Unrolling used to hide this: a view loop over a constant list was unrolled
# for every target and each handler got the element substituted in as a
# literal, capturing nothing. Once a target with a host language emitted the
# loop, the promoted handler referenced a variable that was not in scope and
# examples/calculator stopped building on fyne.

sngl generate --platform=fyne --lang=go --out=fyne app.sngl

# Attached as a closure, in the loop, reading the loop's own variable.
grep 'for _, it := range m.items \{' fyne/model.go
grep 'OnTapped = func\(\) \{' fyne/model.go
grep 'm.picked = it' fyne/model.go
! grep '__n1_click_handler' fyne/model.go

# The closure returns nothing, so it can be assigned to a func() field. It
# used to be emitted as `func() any`, which Go rejected twice over.
! grep 'func\(\) any' fyne/model.go

# The closure's body goes through the platform translator like any other
# statement block: the write to the label is fyne's own setter on the Model
# field, not the raw IR assignment to a bare name it used to be.
grep 'm.__n0.SetText\(m.picked\)' fyne/model.go
! grep '\t*__n0.Text =' fyne/model.go

sngl generate --platform=gtk4 --lang=go --out=gtk app.sngl
grep 'gtk4rt.Connect\(__n1, "clicked", func\(\) \{' gtk/model.go
grep 'm.picked = it' gtk/model.go
! grep '_clicked_handler' gtk/model.go

-- app.sngl --
import . "sngl:ui"

component main {
    var items list<string> = ["a", "b"]
    var picked = ""

    vbox {
        for var it = items {
            button(text=it, @click { picked = it })
        }
    }
    text(value=picked)
}
